description: Phytochemical analysis, standardization of herbal formulations, HPLC/HPTLC profiling, GMP regulations, and clinical validation.

concepts.name: Phytochemical Standardization & Chromatography
concepts.description: Fingerprinting active botanical markers using High-Performance Thin-Layer Chromatography (HPTLC) and HPLC.
concepts.foundational_question: Explain how HPTLC and HPLC fingerprinting are used to standardize polyherbal Ayurvedic formulations (such as Triphala or Ashwagandha extracts) against marker compounds.
targeted_probes: How do you distinguish authentic raw botanical materials from common adulterants using marker compound retention times and spectral matching?
What are the challenges of batch-to-batch variation due to seasonal/geographic harvesting differences, and how do you establish acceptable tolerance limits?

rubric.correctness_criteria: Explains chromatographic separation, retention factor (Rf), and marker quantification (e.g., Withaferin A in Ashwagandha, Gallic acid in Triphala).
rubric.depth_criteria: Details stationary phase, mobile phase selection, UV/MS detection, and limit of quantification (LOQ).
rubric.tradeoff_criteria: Compares whole-extract synergistic profiling vs single-isolate marker standardization.
rubric.applicability_criteria: Applies Pharmacopoeial standards (Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India - API) for quality verification.

learning_resources.title: Phytochemistry & Herbal Drug Standardization
learning_resources.provider: All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA) / NPTEL

concepts.name: Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) & Heavy Metal/Microbial Limits
concepts.description: Schedule T compliance, heavy metal limits (AAS/ICP-MS), pesticide residue, and aflatoxin contamination testing.
concepts.foundational_question: What are the mandatory quality control parameters for classical and proprietary Ayurvedic medicines under Schedule T of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act regarding heavy metals and microbial load?
targeted_probes: What are the permissible limits for Lead, Cadmium, Arsenic, and Mercury under API/WHO guidelines, and how are Bhasmas scientifically detoxified through Shodhana?
How do accelerated stability testing protocols determine the shelf life of Ayurvedic asavas, arishtas, and tailas?

rubric.correctness_criteria: States regulatory limits for heavy metals (Lead <= 10ppm, Arsenic <= 3ppm, etc.) and microbial limits (E. coli, Salmonella absence).
rubric.depth_criteria: Explains spectroscopic analysis (AAS/ICP-MS) and stability testing conditions (ICH/API guidelines: 40C/75% RH).
rubric.tradeoff_criteria: Distinguishes toxic raw heavy metal contamination from scientifically processed organo-metallic Bhasmas.
rubric.applicability_criteria: Formulates SOPs for export-grade compliance (US FDA / EU botanical guidelines).

learning_resources.title: Regulatory Compliance & GMP in AYUSH Industries
learning_resources.provider: Ministry of Ayush / AIIA Training Program
